newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends down but LME stock drop expected.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends down but LME stock drop expected.

text.p: COMEX copper ended slightly weaker as the market took a breather following Wednesday's 2.40 cent surge to a six-month high, but an expected drop in LME stocks Friday should provide support, traders said.
Traders noted two unfilled gaps in the charts for March COMEX, located between 111.40 and 108.00 cents.

"The suggestion is that with two gaps in a row and if they are not filled, it means significantly higher prices," Richard Hirsch of Deutsche Morgan Grenfell said. "We started to fill one gap today, so we will have to see."
March copper settled 0.30 cent weaker at 111.40 cents per pound, traded 113.80 to 110.80 cents.
Although the LME backwardation has eased from its recent high of above $300, it remained firm at $75/$80.
Traders expected LME stocks to fall 3,000 to 10,000 tonnes Friday as the weaker backwardation stopped drawing in any surplus metal and the outflow exceeded inventory going in.

"The low backwardation which is bearish for the cash month, is now being interpreted as bullish for the LME three months," Hirsch said. "On balance, we expect a continuation of outflow of copper from the LME."
